title: Can't foster? 9 ways to help Valley street dogs
desc: You don't have to bring a dog home to help. Here are 9 easy ways to help street dogs in the Rio Grande Valley this week, from sharing posts to giving a ride.
alt: A small tan and black street dog with big ears sitting on concrete and looking up at the camera
html:
Not everyone can bring a dog home, and that's okay. Most Valley street dogs get saved by a whole group of people: the person who stops, the one who shares the post, the one who gives a ride, and the one who drops off a bag of food. Here are 9 ways to help this week without fostering.

1. Share lost and found posts

A share costs nothing and puts a dog in front of people in the right neighborhood. Check the Howlback lost & found board and share any dog from your city. If you find a dog, post them free.

2. Keep a "dog kit" in your car

A slip leash, a bag of treats, a water bottle, and a bowl. It takes up almost no space, and it means you can help the next time a dog is wandering near the road instead of just driving past.

3. Get found dogs scanned for a chip

If you pick up a dog, take them to a vet clinic to get scanned for a microchip. Most clinics do it for free and it only takes a minute. It's the fastest way to get a lost dog home. Here's who to call in your city.

4. Leave out water

Valley heat lasts most of the year. A bowl of clean water in the shade by your gate or business can help a dog more than you'd think.

5. Offer a ride

Fosters and rescues are always looking for someone to drive a dog to a vet visit, a spay or neuter appointment, or an adoption event. Let a local rescue know you're free on weekends. See South Texas rescues.

6. Drop off supplies

Ask a foster or rescue what they're short on before you buy. Things they often need:

  • Dog and puppy food
  • Puppy pads
  • Flea and tick treatment
  • Old towels and blankets, especially before a cold front
  • Leashes, collars, and crates

Need a list to shop from? See our foster must-haves.

7. Spread the word about low-cost clinics

Fewer puppies born on the street is the long-term fix. Low-cost spay, neuter, and vaccine clinics happen all over the Valley. Share upcoming clinics with neighbors who have a dog that isn't fixed yet.

8. Speak up when you see dumping

Dumping a dog is a crime in Texas. If you see it happen, write down the plate, the time, and the place, and call your city's animal control or police.

9. Help pay a foster back

Valley fosters pay out of their own pocket for vet visits, meds, and food. Chip In by Howlback is coming soon: fosters upload their receipts, we verify every one, and anyone can chip in any amount to help pay them back. Get first word when it opens.

Every one of these matters. Pick one, and share this with a friend who loves dogs too. 🐾
sources: Palm Valley Animal Society, Resources for dog fosters
